content.user_title: Check Taiwan Daily Maximum UV Indices
content.value_statement: Daily UV maxima can be confused with current exposure levels. This skill queries CWA station data and explains UV categories while identifying daily maximum values.
actual_capabilities: Guide authenticated retrieval of CWA dataset O-A0005-001 with a curl request limited to 20 seconds.
Select station records by StationID and read UVIndex from records.weatherElement.location[].
Classify UV values into low, moderate, high, very high, and extreme levels using the supplied threshold table.
Provide general sun protection guidance associated with each UV category.
Report authorization failures and dataset lookup problems without inventing UV readings.
Retain station identifiers when names are unavailable and distinguish daily maxima from live readings.
limitations: Requires a CWA open-data API key and network access; unauthenticated requests do not provide the dataset.
Provides daily maximum values, not live observations or hourly forecasts.
Station names require a separate mapping; the skill does not include a station-name lookup table.
Returned values may be stale, and API changes can invalidate the documented endpoint or response structure.

use_cases.title: Review UV exposure before outdoor activities
use_cases.description: Check a selected station daily maximum and its UV category before planning outdoor activity.

use_cases.title: Prepare a station-based visitor briefing
use_cases.description: Summarize a station UV category and general protection guidance without presenting the daily maximum as a live reading.

use_cases.title: Inspect CWA UV dataset responses
use_cases.description: Retrieve authorized station records, interpret string success values, and distinguish authentication failures from missing station data.

prompt_templates.title: Check one station
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the daily maximum UV index for station 466950. Include its category and query time. Never show my API key.

prompt_templates.title: Explain protection guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up station 466920 and explain its UV category and general sun protection guidance. Clearly state this is a daily maximum.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two stations
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare daily maximum UV indices for stations 466920 and 466950. Include categories and query time. Report unavailable records without guessing.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an API response
prompt_templates.prompt: Query O-A0005-001 using my securely stored CWA key. Check string success, locate StationID 466950, and report authentication, schema, or freshness uncertainty.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate retrieval and response interpretation

output_examples.input: Explain the documented sample for station 466950.
output_examples.output: Documented sample from September 19, 2026: station 466950 has UVIndex 11.0, classified as extreme. This is a daily maximum, not a current reading.

output_examples.input: Check a station without a configured API key.
output_examples.output: A CWA open-data API key is required. Register for a free key and configure secure storage. No current UV value was retrieved.

output_examples.input: Explain UVIndex 8.0 when the station name is unavailable.
output_examples.output: Illustrative result: UVIndex 8.0 is very high. Avoid midday outdoor exposure and use sun protection. Report the station identifier without guessing its name.

best_practices: Keep the CWA key in secure storage and prevent credential exposure through command logs, shared process details, repositories, or replies.
Include query time and daily maximum labeling; disclose uncertainty about the date represented by the returned value.
Use verified station mappings and report unavailable data or authentication failures explicitly.
anti_patterns: Presenting a daily maximum or historical sample as a current live UV reading.
Guessing station names, missing values, or results after an API failure.
Pasting API keys or unredacted authenticated request URLs into replies, logs, or commits.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Register for a free key on the CWA open-data platform and provide it through secure storage.

faq.question: Does this provide live UV readings?
faq.answer: No. The documented dataset provides daily maxima, not live observations or hourly forecasts.

faq.question: Which data source does the skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the Central Weather Administration open-data dataset O-A0005-001 through the official HTTPS API.

faq.question: What happens if authorization fails?
faq.answer: The skill explains that the key is missing or invalid. It should not replace the failed request with remembered UV values.

faq.question: Can it identify station names?
faq.answer: Station names require a separate CWA mapping. Without a verified match, the skill reports the station identifier.

faq.question: How are UV categories determined?
faq.answer: The supplied table uses 0-2 low, 3-5 moderate, 6-7 high, 8-10 very high, and 11 or above extreme.
